posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Many of you have seen the card games I made in the past. There is one thing I never liked here: Every picture is perfectly straight up.
So, there is 2 things I would like to achieve:
I want to show a picture in a certain angle. Lets say 30 degrees. Normally I would use the default script call to show images, but how do I make them tilted?
I would love to be able to turn them from 0 degrees to 30 degrees, or 0 degrees to 330 (a.k.a -30) degrees and back.
Is it possible with RPG maker? Any help is welcome.
(I know about the rotate function in MV, but that doesn't allow me to go for 0 degrees to X degrees and back.)

posts.author: alasth
posts.body:
As
@bass2yang
says, you can use
$gameScreen._pictures[1]._angle
,
but if, for example, you set
$gameScreen._pictures[1]._angle = 90 ,
it will instantly change the angle to 90°.
If you want a gradual rotation, you can use rotate:
you say :
(I know about the rotate function in MV, but that doesn't allow me to go for 0 degrees to X degrees and back.)
Click to expand...
But that's not entirely true:
The rotate speed in the event corresponds to the rotation in degrees per frame. So by initializing a rotate and stopping it at the right moment, you can use it:
For example, if you set a speed of 2 and wait 16 frames = 32 degrees.
If you don't want to use it in an event, you can also use it in a script, exemple :
◆ Loop
◆ Script :
Code:
var pic = $gameScreen.picture(1);
  if (pic._angle < 180) {
      $gameScreen.rotatePicture(1, 5); // vitesse
  } else {
      $gameScreen.rotatePicture(1, 0); // stop
      break;
  }
◆ Wait: 1 frame
◆ Repeat

In a sense, it may feel that way at first. I didn't even know what alias (or an interpreter) was until just a few years ago and even then, I didn't fully understand it until just this year.
It just takes a bit of getting used to the syntax and the flow of it. I'd be more than happy to share with you my approach for a quick plugin if you would like.
(This is what I usually do when I am working through code in the first few stages. I patch things and see if it needs improvement and if it is something I can really use. If it is, I'll port it to my main .js document and give it a better name space, parameters, etc.).
And, like other things, it is not the only way to do it.
